items.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with acute bilateral lower abdominal pain and fever of 38.3°C for 2 days. Bimanual pelvic examination elicits marked exquisite pain on lateral motion of the cervix (cervical motion tenderness) and bilateral adnexal tenderness. Urine pregnancy test is negative. What is the recommended outpatient antibiotic regimen according to CDC guidelines?
o: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single dose + Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 14 days + Metronidazole 500 mg PO BID for 14 days
Oral Ciprofloxacin 500 mg single dose + Azithromycin 1 g single dose
Intramuscular Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units single dose
Oral Amoxicillin-clavulanate 625 mg TID for 7 days
items.exp: Current CDC STI Treatment Guidelines recommend intramuscular Ceftriaxone 500 mg as a single dose (to cover N. gonorrhoeae) plus oral Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days (to cover C. trachomatis) plus oral Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 14 days (to cover anaerobes and BV).
r: Correct. Ceftriaxone + Doxycycline + Metronidazole is the evidence-based CDC outpatient regimen for PID.
Incorrect. Fluoroquinolones are no longer recommended due to high widespread gonococcal resistance.
Incorrect. Penicillin G treats Treponema pallidum (syphilis), not polymicrobial PID.
Incorrect. Amoxicillin-clavulanate lacks sufficient activity against Chlamydia trachomatis.
items.kp: The CDC outpatient PID regimen is Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single dose plus Doxycycline and Metronidazole for 14 days.

items.q: A 25-year-old woman with treated pelvic inflammatory disease presents with sharp, pleuritic right upper quadrant pain exacerbated by deep inspiration and coughing. Liver function tests show mildly elevated transaminases, and abdominal ultrasound excludes gallstones. Diagnostic laparoscopy demonstrates thin, delicate 'violin-string' adhesions between the anterior liver capsule and abdominal wall. What is this condition?
items.exp: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis associated with pelvic inflammatory disease, typically caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (or N. gonorrhoeae). Transperitoneal spread leads to inflammation of the liver capsule and produces pathognomonic 'violin-string' adhesions between the liver and anterior parietal peritoneum.
r: Correct. Fibrinous perihepatitis with 'violin-string' adhesions following PID is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.
Incorrect. Budd-Chiari syndrome is hepatic vein thrombosis presenting with hepatomegaly and ascites.
Incorrect. Mirizzi syndrome is extrinsic common bile duct compression by an impacted cystic duct stone.
Incorrect. Caroli disease is congenital dilatation of the intrahepatic bile ducts.
items.kp: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is Chlamydia or gonococcal perihepatitis producing 'violin-string' adhesions and pleuritic RUQ pain.

items.q: A 28-year-old woman complains of a malodorous, grayish-white vaginal discharge that worsens after intercourse. Pelvic examination reveals no erythema. Vaginal pH is 5.2. Addition of 10% potassium hydroxide (KOH) to the discharge produces a strong fishy odor. Wet mount microscopy demonstrates vaginal epithelial cells with stippled borders obscured by adherent bacteria. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: The clinical picture fulfills all four Amsel criteria for bacterial vaginosis: thin homogenous discharge, vaginal pH > 4.5, positive amine whiff test with 10% KOH, and the presence of clue cells (vaginal epithelial cells studded with adherent bacteria, obscuring cell borders) on wet mount microscopy.
r: Correct. Amsel criteria including clue cells, positive whiff test, and pH > 4.5 confirm bacterial vaginosis.
Incorrect. Trichomoniasis features motile flagellates, marked introital erythema, and strawberry cervix.
Incorrect. Candidiasis features curd-like discharge, severe pruritus, pseudohyphae, and normal acidic pH (< 4.5).
Incorrect. Desquamative inflammatory vaginitis features parabasal cells and purulent yellow discharge.
items.kp: Bacterial vaginosis is diagnosed by Amsel criteria: thin discharge, pH > 4.5, positive whiff test, and > 20% clue cells.

items.q: Which of the following findings on pelvic examination is characteristic of Trichomonas vaginalis infection?
o: Punctate macular hemorrhages on the ectocervix ('strawberry cervix')
Curdy white cottage-cheese like adherent plaques
Vesicular lesions on an erythematous base
items.exp: Colpitis macularis, commonly called 'strawberry cervix', characterized by punctate mucosal hemorrhages across the ectocervix and upper vaginal walls, is pathognomonic for Trichomonas vaginalis infection (seen in 2-5% on gross exam and up to 45% on colposcopy).
r: Correct. Strawberry cervix (colpitis macularis) is the classic physical examination finding of trichomoniasis.
Incorrect. Curdy white cottage-cheese plaques are characteristic of Candida albicans.
Incorrect. Painful vesicles on an erythematous base indicate Herpes simplex virus (HSV).
Incorrect. Cervical ectropion is a normal physiological variant.
items.kp: Strawberry cervix (colpitis macularis) is the classic sign of Trichomonas vaginalis infection.

items.q: Why is treating the male sexual partner mandatory in cases of confirmed Trichomonas vaginalis infection, but not routinely recommended in bacterial vaginosis?
o: Trichomoniasis is a true sexually transmitted infection with high male carriage rates and reinfection risk
Bacterial vaginosis bacteria are completely destroyed by male prostatic secretions
Trichomonas cannot survive in women without male reinoculation
Metronidazole is toxic to asymptomatic men in BV
items.exp: Trichomonas vaginalis is an obligate sexually transmitted protozoan where male partners frequently harbor asymptomatic urethral infection. Without simultaneous treatment of all sexual partners, female reinfection rates exceed 20-30%. Bacterial vaginosis is a dysbiosis of native flora, and partner treatment has not consistently reduced recurrence rates in trials.
r: Correct. Trichomoniasis is an STI requiring simultaneous partner treatment to prevent rapid female reinfection.
Incorrect. Prostatic secretions do not destroy BV bacteria.
Incorrect. Trichomonas persists in females independently of reinoculation.
Incorrect. Metronidazole is safe in men and used routinely for male trichomoniasis.
items.kp: Simultaneous partner treatment with oral metronidazole is mandatory in trichomoniasis to prevent reinfection.

items.q: A 24-year-old woman with clinically diagnosed PID is admitted to the hospital due to high fever, peritoneal signs, and ultrasound demonstration of an 8 cm complex cystic adnexal mass with thick walls and internal echoes. Blood cultures are drawn. What is the initial management?
o: Intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics (Cefoxitin + Doxycycline or Clindamycin + Gentamicin)
Immediate exploratory laparotomy and unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
Percutaneous needle drainage without antibiotic coverage
items.exp: A complex cystic adnexal mass in the setting of acute PID represents a tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA). First-line management is inpatient hospitalization and intravenous broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy with activity against anaerobes (e.g., Cefoxitin 2g IV q6h + Doxycycline 100mg IV/PO q12h, or Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h + Gentamicin). Over 70-80% of TOAs respond successfully to medical therapy without surgical excision.
r: Correct. Inpatient broad-spectrum IV antibiotics covering anaerobes is the primary initial therapy for intact TOA.
Incorrect. Immediate laparotomy and oophorectomy is overtreatment for intact TOA, which resolves medically in 80% of cases.
Incorrect. Drainage without antibiotics leads to severe peritonitis and bacteremia.
Incorrect. Methotrexate is a chemotherapeutic agent for ectopic pregnancy, not an abscess treatment.
items.kp: Tubo-ovarian abscess without signs of rupture is managed initially with inpatient broad-spectrum IV antibiotics covering anaerobes.

items.q: Which long-term complication of pelvic inflammatory disease has the highest relative risk increase compared to women without a history of PID?
items.exp: Tubal mucosal damage, endosalpingeal deciliation, and luminal adhesions resulting from PID increase the relative risk of subsequent tubal ectopic pregnancy by approximately 7- to 10-fold compared to uninfected controls. It also causes tubal factor subfertility in 10-20% after one episode and > 40% after three episodes.
r: Correct. Ectopic pregnancy risk increases 7- to 10-fold following PID due to permanent loss of tubal ciliary motility.
Incorrect. Cervical dysplasia is caused by persistent high-risk HPV, not bacterial PID.
Incorrect. Endometrial carcinoma is linked to unopposed estrogen, not infectious salpingitis.
Incorrect. Ovarian fibroma is a benign stromal neoplasm unrelated to infection.
items.kp: A history of PID increases the subsequent risk of tubal ectopic pregnancy by 7- to 10-fold.

items.q: What is the normal vaginal pH in a healthy, asymptomatic reproductive-age woman with intact estrogen levels?
items.exp: Under estrogen stimulation, mature vaginal squamous cells produce glycogen, which is metabolized by Lactobacillus species (predominantly L. crispatus and L. jensenii) into lactic acid and hydrogen peroxide. This maintains a healthy acidic vaginal pH of 3.8 to 4.5, which inhibits pathogenic bacteria.
r: Correct. Normal reproductive-age vaginal pH is 3.8 to 4.5, maintained by lactobacilli-derived lactic acid.
Incorrect. pH > 4.5 is abnormal, characteristic of bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis.
Incorrect. pH 6.5 to 7.2 is near neutral, seen in postmenopausal atrophy or amniotic fluid leakage.
Incorrect. Alkaline pH > 7.5 is highly abnormal.
items.kp: Normal vaginal pH in reproductive-age women is acidic (3.8 to 4.5), maintained by Lactobacillus lactic acid production.

items.q: A 30-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 1 diabetes presents with intense vulval itching and thick, white, curd-like vaginal discharge. Speculum examination shows marked vulval erythema and discharge clinging to the walls. Vaginal pH is 4.0. Microscopy with 10% KOH reveals pseudohyphae and budding yeast forms. What is the first-line treatment?
o: Single oral dose of Fluconazole 150 mg
Oral Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
Oral Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days
items.exp: The clinical presentation (pruritus, curd-like discharge, acidic pH 4.0, pseudohyphae on KOH mount) confirms acute vulvovaginal candidiasis (Candida albicans). First-line oral therapy for uncomplicated candidiasis is a single oral dose of Fluconazole 150 mg (or topical azole regimens like clotrimazole pessaries).
r: Correct. Fluconazole 150 mg orally is the standard first-line treatment for acute vulvovaginal candidiasis.
Incorrect. Metronidazole treats anaerobic bacteria and trichomoniasis, not fungal Candida.
Incorrect. Doxycycline treats Chlamydia and would exacerbate fungal candidiasis by killing bacteria.
Incorrect. Clindamycin is an antibacterial used for bacterial vaginosis.
items.kp: Vulvovaginal candidiasis presents with severe pruritus, curd-like discharge, pH < 4.5, and pseudohyphae, treated with oral fluconazole.

items.q: Which diagnostic finding provides definitive, gold-standard confirmation of acute pelvic inflammatory disease?
o: Diagnostic laparoscopy with visual confirmation of tubal erythema, edema and purulent exudate
Gram stain of endocervical swab showing Gram-negative intracellular diplococci
items.exp: Laparoscopy is the recognized gold standard for the diagnosis of PID, allowing direct visualization of tubal hyperemia, serosal edema, fimbrial agglutination, and purulent exudate flowing from the tubal ostium, as well as enabling targeted microbiological culture and exclusion of acute appendicitis.
r: Correct. Direct laparoscopic visualization of hyperemic, exudative fallopian tubes is the diagnostic gold standard.
Incorrect. Ultrasound is insensitive for mild-to-moderate salpingitis without abscess formation.
Incorrect. CRP is non-specific and elevated in any inflammatory process.
Incorrect. Endocervical Gram stain confirms gonococcal cervicitis, but cannot prove upper tract extension.
items.kp: Diagnostic laparoscopy is the gold standard for diagnosing acute pelvic inflammatory disease.
